name.tagline: I build products end to end: React and Next.js on the front, Go and Node services behind them, and the queues and databases that keep everything up.

about: I'm a full-stack developer, currently interning at InboxKit, where I ship features across the stack for an email infrastructure platform used by outreach teams. I like owning a feature from the interface down: the UI, the API behind it, the data model, and the background jobs that keep it honest.

On the front end that means React and Next.js with TypeScript; behind it, Go for services and workers and Node for APIs, with PostgreSQL, Redis, and Kafka doing the heavy lifting. I started with C/C++ and Codeforces, and still do a bit of DSA in C++.

projects.name: Switchyard
projects.blurb: AI-powered workflow automation for engineering teams. Describe a workflow in natural language, edit the generated graph, then execute it deterministically with visible logs, retries, and live WebSocket events.
projects.role: Workflow engine, Go API, and visual builder
highlights: Go workflow engine with asynchronous execution, retries, cancellation, idempotency keys, and recovery of interrupted runs.
Workspace RBAC, encrypted credential storage, signed webhooks, and SSRF protection.
Integrations with GitHub, Slack, Discord, SMTP, and multiple LLM providers.

projects.name: PulseOps
projects.blurb: Self-hostable uptime and latency monitoring. HTTP and heartbeat checks, incidents, SLA analytics, a web dashboard, a read-only API, and a terminal TUI — the whole stack comes up with one docker compose.
highlights: Concurrent Go ping engine: a goroutine worker pool fed by Kafka, probing HTTP, TCP, DNS, and keyword checks.
Results are deduplicated in Redis and Kafka offsets commit only after they land, so at-least-once delivery never opens a phantom incident.
Webhook alerting with retries and exponential backoff on Redis and BullMQ.

projects.name: AuraMail
projects.blurb: AI placement-email analyzer. Syncs Gmail over OAuth, summarizes with GPT-4 Mini, extracts company, role, deadline and salary, and pushes deadlines to Google Calendar — streamed live over SSE.
projects.role: Go backend, Gmail sync, AI pipeline
highlights: Gmail sync over Google OAuth 2.0 with read-only access, running in the background and grouping related messages into threads.
GPT-4 Mini extracts company, role, deadline, salary, and eligibility from unstructured email.
Go backend streams processing updates over Server-Sent Events; the Postgres schema is managed with Goose migrations.

projects.name: SongSpot
projects.blurb: A collaborative listening room. Share a six-character code and everyone lands on the same second of the same song. The Go server never streams audio — it keeps a playhead anchor in Redis and fans out play, pause and seek over WebSockets, while each browser drives its own YouTube player.
projects.role: Go sync server, Redis pub/sub, React client
highlights: Per-room hubs in Go, with Redis Pub/Sub fanning play, pause, and seek out to every socket in the room.
Playback state is an anchor (a position plus when it was recorded), not a ticking clock; each client works out where the song is now.
Clock-offset estimation over the socket, so listeners with skewed clocks or slow networks still land on the same second.

projects.name: GitHub Banners
projects.blurb: A Go service that renders live SVG banners of GitHub stats. Multi-token rotation for rate limits, layered in-memory and Postgres caching with soft/hard TTLs, Kafka between services, and HMAC-signed internal calls.
highlights: Multi-token rotation keeps the service under GitHub's rate limits.
Two-layer cache, in-memory and Postgres, with a 10-minute soft TTL and a 24-hour hard TTL.
Services talk over Kafka, and internal calls are HMAC-signed.

projects.name: TaskFlow
